title: Vitalik Buterin says AI still can't judge what new writing argues
body: Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has found an area where humans still have a leg up over AI, pointing out an apparent weakness in working out the core argument of newly published literature that has not yet been extensively covered in its training. Vitalik wrote in July that AI was overtaking humans one capability at a time. That assertion came in the same month that an AI tool identified his writing style and named him as the author of an Ethereum document he wrote anonymously. Commentary has framed Vitalik’s latest post as a word of caution to crypto teams and traders who rely on AI summaries instead of reading entire documents such as whitepapers, audits and governance proposals. Vitalik Buterin: Knowledge is different from wisdom Vitalik’s October 29 X post names a capability he thinks humans are still better at than machines, writing that he finds AI “extremely knowledgeable, and so exceptionally able to detect references to almost anything, but not very wise, and so it only makes the most surface-level judgements about what point some writing is making.” The Ethereum co-founder noted that the contrast is especially noticeable when a model is reading the material for the first time. AI models can draw on auxiliary literature and years of human commentary when they evaluate famous texts. With brand-new essays, on the other hand, these chatbots can not access the same level of supporting material, so the model has little to build on other than the words themselves. Vitalik’s remark was prompted by an argument going on X over a Wall Street Journal piece on the demanding Humanities 10 course for Harvard freshmen. One user, arguing that current AI models are already better than humans as discussion partners on the classics, drew a challenge from another user, who said chatbots produce “slop” when they give feedback on her essays, for now. Vitalik’s history with AI text analysis In a June experiment to see whether AI has cracked online anonymity, Vitalik initiated an open challenge to find an Ethereum document he had published anonymously years earlier. Vitalik confirmed that Franklyn Wang’s team at Co-Invest won the contest on July 6. The tool that picked the winner put the odds of Buterin’s authorship at roughly 20% after sifting through 27 texts. The document that Vitalik based the contest on went through multiple rounds that would have obscured the author’s trail. The anonymous rewrite of EIP-7503 was drafted in Chinese, ran through the Qwen 2.5 model locally, before he manually cleaned up the translation. Wang said the model identified the correct document by evaluating reasoning style, such as how Vitalik explains algorithms and technical ideas, rather than vocabulary. Vitalik argued that machines keep surpassing humans one skill at a time rather than all at once, two weeks later, on July 20. Why this matters for crypto teams leaning on AI The practical edge is in crypto security. Vitalik has recently warned that AI could weaken key parts of crypto defenses within two years, and he has backed tools that keep humans in the loop, including a “paranoid mode” for AI chats and an earlier “compute winter button” governance idea. A surface-level read is exactly the failure mode he flags. Teams handing smart-contract audits, research and token-supply schedules to AI agents may get a fluent summary that misses a subtle flaw, because the model is checking references, not weighing an argument it has never seen before. Not everyone agrees with his skepticism. Some investors argue AI already beats top human minds in fields like math. If you're reading this, you’re already ahead. Stay there with our newsletter .

title: NBA Names Kalshi and Polymarket Preferred Prediction Market Exchanges
body: The NBA on October 26 named Kalshi and Polymarket as its Preferred Prediction Market Exchanges, formalising a commercial category for event-contract platforms around its games. The league also announced a memorandum of understanding with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission covering cooperation and information sharing on NBA prediction markets, according to the NBA . The designations give the exchanges access to official league assets while placing the NBA directly in the approval and integrity process for the markets offered on its events. Kalshi and Polymarket receive NBA rights Kalshi and Polymarket, designated as preferred exchanges, will receive NBA intellectual-property and marketing rights and official Sportradar data to operate and settle authorized NBA-related markets under multi-year arrangements, the Associated Press reported . The deals make the exchanges league-approved commercial partners rather than platforms operating NBA-related contracts without a direct league agreement. The NBA retains approval rights over the types of prediction markets offered on its games and said the agreements set limits on permissible NBA markets. Market approval and integrity rules The NBA retains approval rights over the types of prediction markets offered on its games, according to the AP. The league said its agreements also set limits on permissible NBA markets. League and team personnel are prohibited from trading NBA event contracts under the arrangements. The agreements further require information sharing related to suspicious trading and investigations, creating a mechanism for the exchanges and league to coordinate when activity raises integrity concerns. The safeguards are central to the NBA's framework: commercial access to its brand and official data is tied to restrictions on what contracts can be listed and to oversight of trading activity involving its competitions. CFTC MOU and DraftKings expansion The NBA's MOU with the CFTC covers cooperation and information sharing on NBA prediction markets . Separately, the league expanded its agreement with DraftKings to include prediction markets and nationwide promotion. title: DTCC Launches Tokenized Securities Service as Wall Street Tests New Settlement Rails
body: TL;DR: The Depository Trust Company, part of DTCC, launched its tokenization service on October 28, moving a particularly important part of institutional blockchain discussion from experimentation toward live market infrastructure. For digital-asset markets, the launch is a reminder that tokenization may expand blockchain activity without immediately translating into buying pressure for a particular cryptocurrency. The Depository Trust Company, part of DTCC, launched its tokenization service on October 28, moving a particularly important part of institutional blockchain discussion from experimentation toward live market infrastructure. The company says its system creates tokenized representations of securities already held in DTC custody rather than issuing unbacked substitutes. The launch initially integrates the Canton Network and DTCC’s private Besu environment, while further network connections are planned for 2027. This distinction between an existing security and a digital representation of it matters: legal entitlement and the depository’s established controls remain central to the design. The event and the market response DTCC describes the service as a way for authorized participants to move eligible assets between traditional and tokenized environments, with potential uses in collateral mobility, capital efficiency and access to liquidity. The important innovation is not that a stock can appear in a wallet, but that institutions may be able to reuse the same underlying holding in different approved workflows without relying on disconnected records. The company also names a broad ecosystem of technology and market participants working on connectivity, including custody, trading, wallet and application specialists. Launching the service does not mean every asset can immediately circulate everywhere. Why the development matters to the crypto market For digital-asset markets, the launch is a reminder that tokenization may expand blockchain activity without immediately translating into buying pressure for a particular cryptocurrency. Canton and a private Besu deployment serve regulated workflows; neither should be confused with public token speculation. Still, dependable post-trade plumbing could create demand for adjacent services such as onchain cash, identity checks and compliant collateral management. The most interesting question is whether institutions can complete an entire trade lifecycle across the new rails, rather than only hold a mirrored security position. The distinction between a blockchain record and the economic rights behind it is crucial for anyone evaluating this news. Digital tokens may move quickly, but title, custody, investor eligibility and redemption remain governed by legal agreements and regulated entities. A new integration should therefore be judged by the processes it can complete end to end, not simply by the number of assets it can represent. Traders also need to resist treating institutional enthusiasm as an automatic bullish signal for a native cryptocurrency: commercial adoption and token pricing can diverge for long periods. What the headline does not establish Operational details will determine the size of the change. Eligible instruments, transfer restrictions, corporate actions, investor protections, and the availability of a cash settlement leg all shape whether tokenization becomes a practical alternative to established processes. DTCC has presented a staged, interoperable model, not a promise that market hours or regulatory requirements have disappeared. Investors should also distinguish a network going live from widespread transaction volume: institutional access, integrations and real usage can rise at different speeds. Tracking the conversion process and participating firms will be more informative than counting announcements alone. What to watch next The next evidence to look for is the breadth of assets actually used, the pace of participant onboarding, and examples of completed collateral or settlement transactions. Any expansion into additional chains in 2027 should be assessed against operational reliability and regulatory clarity, not treated as automatic adoption. title: WhiteBIT adds USD SWIFT transfers for corporate clients through BCB Group partnership
body: WhiteBIT , a global cryptocurrency exchange , has expanded its institutional payment offering through a partnership with BCB Group, adding USD deposits and withdrawals via SWIFT . The new capability gives KYB-verified corporate clients access to an international USD settlement channel for moving funds between cryptocurrency and fiat markets. The integration targets businesses that need to manage USD liquidity across borders while retaining access to digital asset trading. Corporate clients can use the service for both incoming and outgoing transfers, with a flat transaction fee and transfer capacity determined on an individual basis through verification. “Reliable access to USD liquidity is a cornerstone of institutional crypto adoption,” said Volodymyr Nosov , Founder and President of W Group, which WhiteBIT is a part of. “By offering SWIFT-based USD transfers, we’re providing businesses with a globally recognised settlement rail to manage liquidity more efficiently and scale across markets.” USD remains central to global settlements The US dollar represented roughly half of all SWIFT payments by value in mid-2026, a share that rises to around three-quarters when intra-Eurozone transfers are excluded. For businesses operating internationally, USD settlement infrastructure underpins payments, treasury transfers and liquidity allocation across markets. Businesses active in cryptocurrency markets face the same requirements, particularly when converting digital asset holdings into fiat or settling with traditional financial counterparties. WhiteBIT’s SWIFT integration provides a two-way payment channel built to support these transactions within an institutional account structure. A dedicated channel for corporate treasury The payment rail allows corporate clients to deposit USD into WhiteBIT and withdraw funds through the SWIFT network. This supports use cases including converting cryptocurrency revenue, managing fiat balances, and handling cross-border settlements that involve digital assets. Transfer limits are not fixed in advance. Instead, the amount a client can move is established through Source of Funds verification and individual account assessment, with capacity reflecting each client’s financial profile and compliance requirements. Pricing structure for USD transfers WhiteBIT has set a flat $54 transaction fee for USD SWIFT deposits and withdrawals. The standard conversion fee between fiat and cryptocurrency is 0.1%. Corporate clients with high transaction volumes may be offered individual commercial terms based on their trading and settlement activity. BCB Group’s infrastructure underpins the service The USD settlement channel runs on BCB Group’s infrastructure, which connects cryptocurrency businesses with traditional financial settlement systems and provides banking and payment services for the digital asset sector. The partnership broadens WhiteBIT’s fiat capabilities for corporate users and adds another option for businesses managing international USD liquidity. WhiteBIT serves 10 million users across more than 150 countries and offers over 1,020 trading pairs across more than 360 digital assets. Featured image via WhiteBIT. title: Arbitrum One daily addresses jump 3.5x to 1.09 million, most since mid-2024
body: Arbitrum One registered 1,087,999 daily active addresses on Oct. 28, making it the most active day since July 18, 2024. The count leapt about 3.5 times in one day, from 306,510 on Oct. 27. Growthepie data puts the prior 2026 high at 571,767 on Oct. 21. The new reading is ~90% higher. Only five previous days in growthepie’s Arbitrum series outstripped it, all occurring in 2024. There were four between May 16 and May 19, including the all-time high of 1,488,384 on May 18. The fifth was July 18, 2024, which was the last day the network hit a million addresses. The Oct. 28 total was about 263% more than the median from Oct. 21 to Oct. 27 (299,959). Transactions rose only about 1.7 times on Oct. 28 Transactions did not keep up. On Oct. 28, growthepie counted 2,147,159, up from 1,275,943 the day before, which is about 1.7 times as many. That was about 68% more than the seven-day median. Arbitrum One daily active addresses and transaction count over 90 days through Oct. 28, 2026, on growthepie . Fees paid by users went up from ~$14,971 to ~$19,108, which is only 3% more than the median of ~$18,574 over the prior week. Fees were higher on Oct. 26, at about $21,071. Arbitrum was placed third by active addresses among the chains that growthepie tracked on Oct. 28. Polygon PoS had the most active addresses with 1,634,452, Base came in second with 1,457,258, and Ethereum mainnet came in fourth with 662,738. The number of active addresses on the Ethereum mainnet rose from 568,553 on Oct. 27 to its highest since Sept. 25. From 380,758 on Oct. 27, Polygon PoS’s count rose to its highest level since Dec. 27, 2025. Base went up from 590,927 to the most since Sept. 3, 2025. Rolly went live on Arbitrum with a $70,000 race on Oct. 28 The launch of Rolly, a no-KYC crypto casino, on Arbitrum was on Oct. 28. It said it had added $10 million to a public bankroll and started its first season with a “$70,000 race.” The same day, Arbitrum’s account welcomed it. There is no public link between the number of addresses and Rolly. And Arbitrum has gone up and down earlier this month. On Oct. 23, it had 563,669 active addresses, but by Oct. 25, it had dropped to 97,267. It logged just 95,545 on Sept. 26. Growthepie keeps track of unique sending addresses every day, but not of recipients. Also, one person can have more than one wallet. Growthepie said that sybil behavior, in which fake wallets pretend to be active during incentive campaigns or airdrops, can make the count go up. It suggests the number should be read along with chain revenue or total value secured. The ARB token hasn’t kept up with what’s going on. It fell about 24% in 30 days and hit a four-week low of $0.1638 on Oct. 24, according to Cryptopolitan . ARB was trading at ~$0.168 at 11:10 UTC on Oct. 29, according to CoinGecko , down ~19% over 30 days.
